title: Untangle an email thread into decisions
goal: Identify the latest decision, owner and deadline without treating every suggestion as agreement.
explanation: Threads contain reversals, quoted older messages and different time zones. Work from the most recent relevant message while preserving the decision trail. The aim is a reviewable table, not an automatically sent message. Use fictional correspondence rather than a real private thread.
sampleInput: 09:00 Nia: “Could we launch Friday? Tari, could you check the copy?” 10:00 Tari: “I can check it Thursday by 15:00 CAT.” 11:00 Nia: “Friday is postponed. We need finance approval first.” 12:00 Jo: “I will ask finance today; no launch date is approved yet.”
prompt: Create a table of current action, owner, agreed deadline, status and supporting message/time. Separate proposals, accepted tasks, blockers and superseded decisions. List the main friction points. Do not invent an approved launch date or send any messages.
workedExample: Copy review | Tari | Thursday 15:00 CAT | accepted. Finance inquiry | Jo | today, relative to thread date | accepted. Launch | date not approved | blocked by finance. Friday’s proposed launch is superseded, not still a commitment.

steps.title: Order the messages
steps.text: Record the thread date if known and distinguish message times from task deadlines.

steps.title: Extract current actions
steps.text: Keep owners, statuses and exact supporting quotations.

steps.title: Resolve reversals
steps.text: Mark the Friday proposal superseded rather than leaving two active launch dates.

steps.title: Find missing information
steps.text: Note that “today” needs the actual thread date and that finance has not approved anything.

steps.title: Draft a confirmation
steps.text: Write a review-only summary asking for the missing date, not a claim that the project is ready.

checks: The latest no-approved-launch-date decision supersedes the Friday suggestion.
Accepted tasks retain the correct owner and deadline, including time zone.
Relative dates and missing approvals stay unresolved instead of being guessed.
commonMistakes: Copying the oldest quoted suggestion as the current decision.
Turning an assigned inquiry into an approved business outcome.
offline: Make an action ledger manually from the four time-stamped messages.
reflection: Which sentence changed the project state rather than merely adding information?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. The latest no-approved-launch-date decision supersedes the Friday suggestion.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Accepted tasks retain the correct owner and deadline, including time zone.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Copying the oldest quoted suggestion as the current decision.
